hints: Intense geomagnetic storm: Dst minimum -146 nT.
Dst first fell below -50 nT 7 hours before reaching its minimum.
Dst was back above -30 nT 17 hours after the minimum.
Sustained southward Bz: 14 hours at or below -5 nT; minimum hourly Bz -19.7 nT.
Ordinary solar wind speed: maximum hourly speed 400 km/s.
High solar wind dynamic pressure: up to 13.4 nPa (protons only).
Strong solar wind electric field: vBs up to 7.6 mV/m.

caveats: All values are hourly means in UTC; minute-level extremes are larger.
Solar wind and magnetic field values are shifted to the time they reach Earth (a delay of roughly 25 to 100 minutes depending on solar wind speed).
Bz is in GSM coordinates; negative Bz means southward.

claims_requiring_a_retrieved_source: physical cause of the event (for example a coronal mass ejection or a high-speed stream)
impacts on satellites, GNSS, radio communication, power grids or aurora
comparison with, or ranking against, other historical storms
